courses.title: Indian Polity Basics
courses.subtitle: The Constitution, Parliament, President and courts, explained simply for exams and everyday understanding.
courses.description:
A fast, exam-friendly introduction to how India is governed.

## Covered

- How the Constitution was made, and its key features
- Fundamental Rights and Duties
- Parliament: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
- The President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
- The Supreme Court and High Courts

Good for UPSC, SSC, state PSC and banking aspirants, and anyone curious.

lessons.title: Making of the Constitution
lessons.summary: Who wrote it, how long it took, and when it came into force.
lessons.content:
## Quick facts

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| Constituent Assembly first met | 9 December 1946 |
| President of the Assembly | Dr Rajendra Prasad |
| Chairman, Drafting Committee | Dr B. R. Ambedkar |
| Adopted | 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) |
| Came into force | 26 January 1950 (Republic Day) |
| Time taken | 2 years, 11 months, 18 days |

## Borrowed features

- **UK**: parliamentary system, rule of law
- **USA**: Fundamental Rights, judicial review
- **Ireland**: Directive Principles of State Policy
- **Canada**: federation with a strong centre

### Remember

26 January was chosen because on that day in 1930 the Congress declared *Purna Swaraj* (complete independence).

lessons.title: Fundamental Rights and Duties
lessons.summary: The six Fundamental Rights (Part III) and the eleven Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A).
lessons.content:
## Six Fundamental Rights (Part III)

1. **Right to Equality** (Articles 14–18)
2. **Right to Freedom** (Articles 19–22)
3. **Right against Exploitation** (Articles 23–24)
4. **Right to Freedom of Religion** (Articles 25–28)
5. **Cultural and Educational Rights** (Articles 29–30)
6. **Right to Constitutional Remedies** (Article 32)

Dr Ambedkar called **Article 32** the "heart and soul" of the Constitution.

The Right to Property was originally a Fundamental Right; the 44th Amendment (1978) made it a legal right under Article 300A.

## Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, Article 51A)

Added by the **42nd Amendment (1976)** on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation. There were 10; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th: parents' duty to provide education to children aged 6–14.

lessons.title: Parliament: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
lessons.summary: Composition, terms and powers of the two Houses.
lessons.content:
Parliament = **President + Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha** (Article 79).

| | Lok Sabha | Rajya Sabha |
|---|---|---|
| Also called | House of the People | Council of States |
| Max strength | 550 (currently 543 elected) | 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated) |
| Term | 5 years (can be dissolved) | Permanent; one-third retire every 2 years |
| Member term | 5 years | 6 years |
| Minimum age | 25 | 30 |
| Presiding officer | Speaker | Vice-President (Chairman) |

## Money Bills

Can be introduced **only in the Lok Sabha**. The Rajya Sabha can delay a Money Bill for at most **14 days**.

posts.title: Our Solar System: 15 Facts Worth Knowing
posts.excerpt: From the hottest planet to the longest day, quick facts about our cosmic neighbourhood.
posts.content:
1. The Sun holds about **99.86%** of the Solar System's mass.
2. **Venus** is the hottest planet (about 465 °C), hotter than Mercury, because of its thick CO₂ atmosphere.
3. A day on **Venus** (243 Earth days) is longer than its year (225 Earth days).
4. **Jupiter** is the largest planet; more than 1,300 Earths would fit inside it.
5. **Saturn** is less dense than water.
6. **Mars** has the tallest volcano known, **Olympus Mons**, about 22 km high.
7. **Uranus** rotates on its side, tilted about 98°.
8. **Neptune** has the fastest winds recorded on any planet, over 2,000 km/h.
9. **Pluto** was reclassified as a dwarf planet in **2006**.
10. Sunlight takes about **8 minutes 20 seconds** to reach Earth.
11. The **Moon** is moving away from Earth by about 3.8 cm a year.
12. **Mercury** has no moons, and neither does Venus.
13. The **asteroid belt** lies between Mars and Jupiter.
14. **Ganymede** (Jupiter) is the largest moon in the Solar System, bigger than Mercury.
15. India's **Chandrayaan-3** landed near the Moon's south pole on **23 August 2023**, a first for any country.

posts.title: How the Internet Actually Works
posts.excerpt: What happens in the second between typing a web address and seeing the page.
posts.content:
## 1. DNS: finding the address

Computers find each other by **IP address** (like `142.250.183.14`). The **Domain Name System** turns a name such as `example.com` into that number, like a phone book.

## 2. Packets

Data is split into small **packets**. Each travels separately, possibly by different routes, and they're reassembled at the end. **TCP** makes sure nothing is lost; **IP** handles the addressing.

## 3. Undersea cables

About **99%** of intercontinental internet traffic travels through **undersea fibre-optic cables**, not satellites.

## 4. HTTPS

The padlock in your browser means the connection is encrypted with **TLS**, so others on the network can't read or change what you send.

### Did you know?

The first message sent over ARPANET, the internet's ancestor, in **1969** was meant to be "LOGIN". The system crashed after "LO".

posts.title: India's National Symbols at a Glance
posts.excerpt: Flag, emblem, anthem, animal, bird and more: the official symbols of India and their stories.
posts.content:
| Symbol | Official choice | Note |
|---|---|---|
| National flag | Tiranga | Adopted 22 July 1947; 24-spoke Ashoka Chakra in navy blue |
| National emblem | Lion Capital of Ashoka, Sarnath | Adopted 26 January 1950; motto *Satyameva Jayate* |
| National anthem | *Jana Gana Mana* | By Rabindranath Tagore; about 52 seconds |
| National song | *Vande Mataram* | By Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay |
| National animal | Bengal tiger | Replaced the lion in 1973 |
| National bird | Indian peafowl (peacock) | |
| National flower | Lotus | |
| National tree | Banyan | |
| National river | Ganga | Declared in 2008 |
| National aquatic animal | Ganges river dolphin | Declared in 2009 |
| National calendar | Saka calendar | Adopted 22 March 1957 |

### Quick quiz

Which article of the Constitution describes the Union's official language? **Article 343**: Hindi in Devanagari script.

posts.title: 7 Wonders of the World (New) and Where They Are
posts.excerpt: The New Seven Wonders chosen in 2007, plus the one ancient wonder still standing.
posts.content:
In **2007**, the New7Wonders Foundation announced the results of a worldwide public vote.

| Wonder | Country | Built |
|---|---|---|
| Taj Mahal | India | 1632–1653 |
| Great Wall | China | 7th century BCE onwards |
| Petra | Jordan | c. 4th century BCE |
| Colosseum | Italy | 70–80 CE |
| Chichén Itzá | Mexico | c. 600–1200 CE |
| Machu Picchu | Peru | c. 1450 CE |
| Christ the Redeemer | Brazil | 1922–1931 |

The **Great Pyramid of Giza**, the only surviving wonder of the ancient world, was given honorary status.

### Fact

The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal emperor **Shah Jahan** in memory of his wife **Mumtaz Mahal**, and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site since **1983**.
